newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico left attacks PAN for backing government laws.
newsitem.headline: Mexico left attacks PAN for backing government laws.

text.p: Mexico's main left-wing opposition on Thursday accused its conservative opposition rivals of being government lackeys who voted in Congress with the long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).
Voters have deserted the PRI in droves because of mounting corruption and bungled economic management over the past 2 1/2 years.

Both major opposition parties hoped to cash in on the discontent in key congressional and governors' elections on July 6, when the PRI may lose its 68-year-old majority in the lower house of Congress.

The left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD), presented a study to reporters on Thursday claiming that the right-wing National Action Party (PAN) had backed more than 85 percent of the bills presented to Congress by the PRI during the 1988-94 presidency of Carlos Salinas de Gortari and the first years of current President Ernesto Zedillo.
"The PAN voted in favour of 85.6 per cent of the laws during the whole Salinas term and in the period so far of Ernesto Zedillo's government," said PRD deputy Mauro Gonzalez.
"National Action can say they are a real opposition but the facts show that the PRI and the PAN go hand in hand and support the same ideas," he added.
The allegation is sensitive because Salinas has fallen into disgrace after ending his term and most voters take a very dim view of anyone who associated with him.

Asked about the PRD's charges, a PAN spokesman said his party had indeed backed many important Salinas reforms -- such as allowing the church legal status or giving the central bank autonomy -- but did so because they corresponded to long-standing party policies.
"We never voted in favour of the PRI's budget or spending plans, not once," the spokesman said.
Another PRD deputy, Adrian Luna, claimed however that "the results reflect the unnatural alliance and the collusion which has always existed between the PAN and the government."
Ironically, the PRD has itself been attacked by the PAN for colluding with the PRI.

Several PRD leaders, including current national president Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador and Mexico City mayoral candidate Cuauhtemoc Cardenas, were former PRI officials who quit the party in the last 10 years.
This has led the PAN to charge that the PRD is little more than a "1970s model PRI."
